name: State-Variable Cost Distribution
description: The original problem exposed a massive affordance by separating the final metric into a sequence-dependent state variable (total idle delay) and a sequence-independent global constant (sum of all p2 values). LLMs perfectly pattern-matched this to the standard two-machine flow shop makespan structure. To defeat this without altering the underlying mathematics, I distributed the global constant into the per-step state updates. By having the state machine accumulate both the dynamic grid draw (idle delay) and the p2 value at every step, the final metric remains mathematically identical (due to commutativity of addition), but structurally it appears as a fully dynamic per-step cost function. This forces the model to actually analyze the state transitions rather than factoring out the constant and defaulting to a known algorithm.
